theme: The Davidic Covenant, the throne, the son, the kingdom forever
readingInstruction: Read 2 Samuel 7:1-29. This is the pivotal chapter of the books of Samuel and one of the most important in the whole Bible. Read it slowly, twice if you can. It is the anchor of this unit.
settingTheScene: David is settled in his palace in Jerusalem, and the LORD has given him rest from his enemies. He feels it is wrong that he lives in a house of cedar while the ark dwells in a tent. He tells the prophet Nathan that he wants to build a house for God. God responds, through Nathan, with a promise that turns David’s plan inside out. This is the Davidic covenant.
observation: David says, “See now, I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of God dwells in a tent” (7:2).
The LORD says, “Would you build me a house to dwell in?… I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep, that you should be prince over my people Israel” (7:5-8).
“I will make for you a great name, like the name of the great ones of the earth” (7:9).
“The LORD declares to you that the LORD will make you a house” (7:11).
“I will raise up your offspring after you… and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever” (7:12-13).
“I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son. When he commits iniquity, I will discipline him with the rod of men” (7:14).
“But my steadfast love will not depart from him” (7:15).
“And your house and your kingdom shall be made sure forever before me. Your throne shall be established forever” (7:16).
interpretation:
David’s desire is good. He wants to honor God. But God’s reply reverses the direction. David wants to build a house for God, and God says that he will build a house for David. The word “house” is used in two senses: a building and a dynasty. God will give David a lasting line of kings. The initiative belongs to God, and the covenant is one of pure promise. David has done nothing to earn it. He was a shepherd, and God made him a king.

The promises are staggering. A great name. A place for Israel, secure from enemies. A son who will build the temple. And above all, a throne established forever. Verse 13 says that God will establish the throne of the kingdom “forever,” and verse 16 repeats it. This is a promise that no human king can fulfill by himself, for every king dies. Even Solomon, the immediate son, will fall. The promise points to a royal line that does not end, and ultimately to a king who lives forever.

Verse 14 is also important. The king is called God’s son: “I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son.” This echoes Psalm 2. It is a statement about the closeness between God and the Davidic king. If the king sins, he will be disciplined, but the covenant will not be cancelled. This differs from Saul. God’s steadfast love is the basis. The promise is unconditional in its ultimate outcome and personal in its fatherly discipline.

David’s prayer in response is one of the most beautiful in Scripture. He goes in and sits before the LORD, and says, “Who am I, O Lord GOD, and what is my house, that you have brought me thus far?” He is overwhelmed. He praises God’s greatness and his choosing of Israel. And he ends with a humble request: “Do as you have promised.” He rests on the word of God.

In the larger story, this chapter is the pivot. All the earlier covenants, with Abraham, with Israel at Sinai, narrow now to a king from David’s line. All the later prophecy points to this son of David. The Bible becomes the story of the search for the promised King.
connection: The New Testament opens with “the book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David” (Matthew 1:1). Gabriel tells Mary that “the Lord God will give to him the throne of his father David, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever” (Luke 1:32-33). Peter says that David “being a prophet… foretold the resurrection of the Christ” (Acts 2:30-31). Hebrews 1:5 quotes 2 Samuel 7:14 of Jesus. Revelation 22:16: “I am the root and the descendant of David.”
application:
Read David’s prayer in verses 18 to 29 aloud as your own prayer of thanksgiving.

Ask where you are trying to do something for God when he is asking you to receive something from him.

Thank God that the throne of David is held forever by Jesus.
prayerPrompts: Tell God what it means that he has brought you this far.
Thank him for the promise to David and its fulfillment in Jesus.
Ask him to establish what he has begun in you.
